[RCLI.1.4] **`compile-project` builds a sketch.** Its argument names a sketch
directory, which must contain a `rules/` directory holding at least one `.ds`
file; if it does not, the invocation fails with exit `2` ([RCLI.3.1]).

Every `.ds` file under `rules/`, at any depth, is compiled as `compile` would
compile it — its imports resolved against the `-L` search path, its dialect
selected by its own `use` directive — and its `.dsc` is written beside it under
the same basename. Unless `--no-header` is given, each artefact is also written
beside it as `<basename>_dsc.h`, in the embedded form [NGST.4.3] states, for a
target that cannot read files.

A module that cannot be read or does not compile does not stop the others.
Every module is attempted, and the exit code is `1` if any failed.
An internal compiler error ends the invocation at once with `3`
([RCLI.3.1]); the artefacts already written for earlier modules stay.
